# The folder and the window {#the-folder-and-the-window .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
Section 1
:::

::: notes
Section one is about the shape of the window. Positron works on a folder, so we start by opening the folder of the workspace and letting R start inside it. Then the seven parts of the window, under the names by which the documentation of Positron describes each part, so that you can find a pane when I name it. Then the files of the workspace, what each file is for and which files you can leave alone, and a first task in which you do all of this on your own machine.
:::

## Opening the folder {#opening-the-folder .smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
::: {.small}
- **File → Open Folder…** (Ctrl+K, then Ctrl+O), and select the folder `replication-lab-housing-main` itself, not a file inside it
- The Explorer lists the files of the folder, and R starts in a console whose **working directory** is that folder, so that `data/housing_audit.csv` finds the file
- The button at the top right names the R that runs the session, with a circle that is green while R is idle and blue while it is busy
:::
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
![](../tools/images/ide/02-file-open-folder.png){fig-alt="The File menu of Positron, with Open Folder highlighted beside its shortcut Ctrl+K Ctrl+O." height="400px" style="border: 1px solid #c9ced4; box-shadow: 1px 1px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.15);"}
:::
::::

::: notes
Positron works on a folder, and the course works in one folder, the unzipped workspace. File, Open Folder, or Control and K followed by Control and O, then choose the folder itself rather than a file inside it, and press Select Folder. Two things happen at once. The files of the folder appear in the Explorer on the left, and R starts in a console whose working directory is that folder, so that a path such as data slash housing audit dot csv finds its file without further ado. Positron starts R by itself when the folder holds R files, and the workspace does. The button at the top right of the window, the interpreter picker, names the version of R that runs your code, which is the first thing to check when a result differs from the one in the course. RStudio users open the dot Rproj file instead, which does the same.
:::

## The parts of the window {#the-parts-of-the-window .smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="74%"}
![](../tools/images/ide/07-window-parts.png){fig-alt="The whole Positron window with seven parts outlined and numbered: the Activity Bar, the Explorer, the editor with the working script, the Console under it, the Variables and Plots panes on the right, the interpreter picker at the top and the Status Bar at the bottom." style="border: 1px solid #c9ced4; box-shadow: 1px 1px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.15);"}
:::
::: {.column width="26%"}
::: {.fs-70 .nonincremental}
1. **Activity Bar** – switches the side bar
2. **Primary Side Bar** – the Explorer, with the files
3. **Editor** – a tab for each open file
4. **Panel** – the Console, beside the Terminal
5. **Secondary Side Bar** – Variables, Plots, Help, Viewer
6. **Top Bar** – search, and the interpreter picker
7. **Status Bar** – Quarto, the cursor, the language
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
This is the whole window with the workspace open, as it looks after the steps of the next section, with its seven parts numbered as the documentation of Positron names them. The strip of icons down the far left, the Activity Bar, switches what the side bar beside it shows, most of the time the Explorer with your files. The editor fills the middle, with a tab for each open file. Under it, the Panel holds the Console, in which R runs, beside the Terminal. On the right, the Secondary Side Bar holds the views of the R session: the Variables and Plots panes, and the Help and Viewer tabs. Along the top run the search box and the interpreter picker, and along the bottom the Status Bar. RStudio users will recognise their four panes: the editor does the work of the Source pane, and the Variables pane that of the Environment tab.
:::

## The files of the workspace {#the-files-of-the-workspace .smaller}

::: {.small}
- `index.qmd` – the report, with Tasks 1 to 5 of the exercise and the preregistration block
- `working_script.R` – the same steps as a plain script, for working in the console
- `R/` – the check script, the starter file of the causal graph, and the helpers of Tasks 4 and 5
- `data/` – the data of the field experiment in which the original authors (OAs) emailed public housing authorities in the United States [@EinsteinGlick2017DoesRaceAffect], each file beside its codebook
- `prep/` – a script that runs all five reanalyses of Task 3 at once
- The rest can be left alone: `_freeze/`, `.github/`, `.devcontainer/` and the `.Rproj` file, which serve the route to a repository of your own and to RStudio
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Every part of the window can be resized by dragging its edge, and hidden and shown again: Ctrl+B for the side bar on the left, Ctrl+Alt+B for the one on the right, Ctrl+J for the Panel.
:::

::: notes
The Explorer shows the workspace as you received it. index dot qmd is the report, with the five tasks of the exercise of the case and the preregistration block, and the last session of today takes it apart. working script dot R holds the same steps as a plain script, for working in the console. The R folder holds the check script, the starter file for the causal graph and the helpers of the later tasks, and the data folder holds the data files of the case, each beside its codebook. The prep folder holds a script that runs all five reanalyses of Task 3 at once. The rest serves the route from the workspace to a repository of your own, and can be left alone. [advance] Sooner or later you will hide a part of the window by accident, so it is worth knowing the three keys that bring the parts back.
:::

## Hands-on 1 – The folder and the window {#hands-on-1-the-folder-and-the-window .smaller}

::: {.small}
1. Open the folder of the workspace, and wait for the console to report that R has started
2. In the Explorer, unfold `data` and `R`. Click `working_script.R` once, and then double-click it, so that it stays open
3. Press Ctrl+J twice, to hide the Panel and bring it back
4. Click the interpreter picker at the top right, read which R runs your code, and press Esc
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
RStudio or VS Code: open the folder in your IDE, and find the files, the console and the version of R.
:::

::: notes
Your turn. Open the folder, if you have not already, and wait until the console says that R has started. Unfold the data and R folders in the Explorer. Click the working script once and notice that the name on its tab is in italics, which marks a preview that the next file you click will replace; double-click it, or start typing in it, to keep it open. Press Control and J twice, to hide the Panel and bring it back. And click the interpreter picker to read which R runs your code, then press Escape. [advance] If you work in RStudio or VS Code, do the same in your own IDE: open the folder, and find the files, the console and the version of R. Take the time you need.
:::
